doc: THE VENDORED UNIT — what a second product copies out of this repository.
ADR 0001 decision 3: the engine and the deck are vendored by pinned tag plus
SHA-256, the discipline tools/fetch-vendor.sh already applies to ONNX Runtime.
Decision 4: the unit sits behind a Host seam, and the engine and the deck must
not know which Host they run under. This file is the declaration of that
boundary, and tools/unit-check.mjs is the gate that holds the tree to it.
Every path here is relative to extension/, the directory Chrome loads. The
layout is part of the contract: workers/workerbackend.js reaches the
inference worker with new URL('./inference.worker.js', import.meta.url), so
a vendoring copy that flattens or renames directories does not run. The
gate follows that form as a reference, which is why inference.worker.js is
not listed as a root: it is reachable, and a rename of it is an unresolved
reference rather than a hand-written path that quietly stopped matching.
workerbackend.js IS a root, for the opposite reason: since S6 (#8) its only
importer in the tree is offscreen/host.js, a declared hole, so a crawl that
stops where a hole starts — which is what a hole means — misses it, and with
it the worker, engine/demucs.js and the whole tensor contract. It is the
Host's choice of backend and the unit's implementation of one at the same
time; its own header says a computed closure must seed it explicitly, and
this is where that is done.
THE LAST THREE SECTIONS ARE ABOUT RUNNING THE UNIT RATHER THAN COPYING IT.
`suites` names the plain-Node suites whose subject is the unit and gives each
one the tools/verify.mjs step id that runs it; `node tools/verify.mjs --unit`
builds its plan from that list, so a suite is gated by being declared here
and by nothing else. `runners` names the files that plan needs to run at all.
`otherSteps` names every remaining step in the runner with the one line that
says why it is not the unit's — present so the classification is TOTAL: a new
suite lands on one side or the gate asks which, the same discipline the
partition at the end of tools/unit-check.mjs applies to files under
extension/. THEIR `path`s ARE REPO-RELATIVE, not extension-relative, because
eight of the fourteen live outside extension/ and a suite is not a thing
Chrome loads. `reads` inside them is spelt extension-relative like every
other path in this file, because everything it can name is declared above.
WHAT A COPY CAN ACTUALLY RUN, SAID HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED.
`--unit` is the plan THIS repository runs over the unit. It is not yet a plan
a second Host passes unchanged, and #11 measured both reasons rather than
describing them as smaller than they are.
One: three suites and one runner reach across the seam. Their `reads` name
seven reads over five files, and the three Host-side ones —
offscreen/host-pin.js, content.js, speed.js — do not travel. Two: `unit` is
ALSO this Host's conformance suite. test.js's group('host') installs a Chrome
platform and asserts that offscreen/host.js and ui/host.js behave, so a
second product that supplies its own holes — which it must; they are holes —
takes 125 assertions RED about a platform it does not have, not a
missing-file error. That one is declared per entry as `hostConformance` and
gated both ways.
Closing either is a decision rather than a bug fix, and they are separate
decisions: the three Host files travel with the copy or the reads that need
them fail, AND group('host') becomes a step of its own under `otherSteps` or
a second Host cannot pass `unit`. S11 (#12) takes both, and docs/VENDORING.md
records what was decided.
WHAT A COPY DOES WITH `otherSteps`: nothing. It is this repository's
inventory of its own harness — the eleven steps whose subject is not the
unit — and it is here because the classification has to be TOTAL for the gate
to catch a new suite nobody classified. A vendoring product's harness has its
own steps and does not inherit these; it may prune the section outright. Said
out loud because S11 (#12) freezes this file as the unit's public surface,
and a section that ships without a stated purpose gets one invented for it
later.
JSON has no comments, so every entry carries its own `why`. Read them: they
are the argument for the classification, and the classification is what the
gate enforces.

entries.why: The engine's orchestration. Host-agnostic since S1; imports its platform surface from ./host.js, which is a hole. The extension reaches it through offscreen/offscreen.html; a second Host supplies its own page and loads this same module.

The deck. Its markup is part of the unit, not of the Host: embed.html's CSP is script-src 'self', so the deck cannot be booted by an inline boot(host) and the page has to carry its own <script>. Everything the deck needs from a Host arrives through ./host.js.

roots.why: An AudioWorklet module, reached by addModule(host.assetUrl(...)). Worklets have no import statements and nothing imports them.
The playback worklet, same reachability. It also carries a verbatim copy of engine/pitch.js and engine/pitchbank.js, because an AudioWorklet has no module system.
The master-bus meter worklet, same reachability.

A DSP module with no importer at all: it is copied verbatim into offscreen/playback-processor.js and it is the copy that runs. The source is the one that can be checked (node extension/engine/pitchbank.js), so it travels with the unit.

Backend #1 — the unit's own implementation of the Backend the EngineHost hands over, and the only file in the unit whose sole importer is a hole (offscreen/host.js imports it; nothing else in the tree does). Seeded here because a crawl that stops at the hole misses it AND everything below it: workers/inference.worker.js, engine/demucs.js, the tensor names and the six-stem layout — the most unit-ish code in the repository, sitting behind the one edge a crawl must not follow. ADR 0001 decision 3 names it for the same reason, and workers/workerbackend.js's own header says a computed closure must seed it explicitly. It is a root, not an entry: an entry is a thing a Host loads, and no Host loads this — the Host CHOOSES it.

holes.why: The extension's EngineHost: send, onMessage, assetUrl, captureStream, modelBytes/modelCached/clearModel. The one module offscreen/engine.js imports that a second product replaces wholesale. Typedefs and the boot-time assertHost live in shared/host.js, which is unit.
The extension's DeckHost: send, onMessage, storage, armShortcut, transport, page. The one module ui/embed.js imports that a second product replaces wholesale.

external.why: ONNX Runtime Web. Not in git, not in the unit, and not this project's code: fetched at a pinned version and verified against a recorded SHA-256 by tools/fetch-vendor.sh. A vendoring product runs that script rather than copying the drop. The crawl stops at this prefix — walking 27 MB of minified runtime looking for `chrome.` would only ever produce a false red.

hostReads.why: The ONE place a unit file reaches a Host file, declared because it is real rather than because it is fine. ui/embed-state.js:2086-2099 reads speed.js AS TEXT — the read is at :2089 — new URL('../speed.js', import.meta.url) — to pin the deck's speed ladder against the content script's clamp: the ladder decides what the user can ASK for, speed.js's clamp decides what the element can BE GIVEN, and a disagreement is a button that visibly moves the readout to a rate the page refuses. It is not an import and nothing in a browser runs it: the read is inside demo(), which runs only under `node extension/ui/embed-state.js`. S10 (#11) DECIDED IT: the check stays behind, and speed.js does not move. Moving it would put a content script that drives the page's <video> inside a unit forbidden to know its Host — decision 4 in the other direction. What that costs a copy is bounded and loud rather than silent: the catch at :2095-2096 turns an unreadable speed.js into `unreadable: ENOENT …` and FEEDS IT TO THE COMPARISON (:2093 is the `};` that closes `grab`, and #11's review caught the citation being off by two), so the ladder assertion goes red naming the file, and it never excuses itself on the file being absent. S11 (#12) decides in docs/VENDORING.md whether a copy carries speed.js for this one pin or takes the red; either way nothing here reports coverage it does not have. It is not the only such read — see `suites` below, where the two larger ones are declared.

host.why: MV3 service worker: the arm gesture, the tabCapture grant, the offscreen document. ADR 0001 decision 4 — only this context can do any of it.
The content script that mounts the deck and owns the page's <video>. It is the other end of every transport and page duty the DeckHost declares.
The setup page. ADR 0001 decision 4 lists ui/welcome* as host-side, and it is: it exists to explain how to arm THIS product in THIS browser.
The setup page's markup. Host-side with its script.

A classic content script — YouTube's autoplay-next suppression. Host-side, and it speaks no chrome.* at all: `node extension/autonav.js` is a verify step, so a chrome. reference at module scope here would take that step out at import.
A classic content script — the page-speed transport and the ad gate. Host-side, and quiet for the same reason autonav.js is: `node extension/speed.js` is a verify step.

Where THIS Host gets the model bytes and where it keeps them: the URL and the Cache API bucket. Host-side because fetching bytes is a Host's duty; the SHA-256 and the byte count stay in shared/config.js because deciding whether the bytes are the model is the unit's. It must stay quiet: tools/host.mjs and tools/fetch-model.sh import it under plain node.

The MV3 offscreen document — the page this Host creates to give the engine an AudioContext. A second Host supplies its own page and loads offscreen/engine.js into it, which is why the entry is the module and not this file.
The extension's declaration of itself. ADR 0001 decision 4 names it host-side; ADR 0001 decision 2 is why it stays that way — no downloads permission, one arm chord.

outside.why: This file. It is the unit's manifest rather than code the unit runs: a vendoring product reads it to know what to copy, and S11 (#12) DECIDED THAT IT IS HASHED alongside what it names, in extension/unit.sha256: it is the first file a vendoring product opens and the one that says what everything else must be, so a copy that verified every file against a manifest it had taken on faith would have checked its own homework. SINCE S10 (#11) IT IS ALSO READ AT RUN TIME — tools/verify.mjs opens it at module scope to build the `--unit` plan — so it travels whether or not it is hashed, and a copy without it has no `--unit`. A TRAP FOR WHOEVER MOVES IT: the `why` strings in this file discuss chrome.* in prose, JSON has no comments to hide them in, and tools/unit-check.mjs classifies a .json file as js, where a string is executable by design. The moment this path leaves `outside`, the gate goes red on the declaration itself — a false red in the safe direction, but the first one to read looks like a real seam breach.

One SHA-256 per unit file, in `shasum -c` format, written by tools/unit-hash.mjs and gated by tools/unit-check.mjs. Outside for the same reason unit.json is: it is ABOUT the unit rather than part of it, and a copy verifies WITH it rather than running it. It hashes unit.json — see that entry — and it does not hash itself, which no sums file can; the tag is what authenticates it. S11 (#12) added it, answering the question the entry above asks.

A suite, not shipped code: it runs the deck's display laws under plain node. It exercises the unit but is not part of it, which is why it is BOTH here and in `suites` below — the two lists answer different questions, and this is the only file under extension/ that needs both answers. `outside` says it does not travel as unit; `suites` says `node tools/verify.mjs --unit` runs it. S10 (#11) added the second half.

required.why: ADR 0001 decision 3, verbatim. Whole-directory rather than a hand list, so a new DSP module that nothing imports fails this gate instead of silently missing the next tag.
ADR 0001 decision 3, verbatim. Whole-directory for the same reason. shared/config.js is the constants and the model's identity; shared/host.js is the Host interface itself.

required.adr: the audio graph in extension/offscreen/ (deck.js, live.js, master.js, cacheddeck.js, the worklet processors)
required.why: Named rather than taken wholesale, because extension/offscreen/ is the one directory with files on both sides of the seam: host.js and host-pin.js are the Host. offscreen/engine.js is the file ADR 0001 wrote as offscreen.js, before S1 split the chrome half out of it.

required.adr: extension/workers/ — inference.worker.js and, since S6 (#8), workerbackend.js
required.why: ADR 0001 decision 3, verbatim, including the sentence S6 added to it. Named rather than taken wholesale for the reason the ADR gives in the same breath: neither file is reachable by import from the unit's entry point, so an enumeration is the only thing that can carry them — inference.worker.js because new URL(..., import.meta.url) is not an import, workerbackend.js because its one importer is a hole.

ADR 0001 decision 3 says embed*.js; the deck as it actually ships is that plus the markup it cannot be booted without, its two stylesheets, and ui/audio-math.js, which is the deck's display maths under a name the glob misses.

hostConformance.why: THE ONE ENTRY IN THIS LIST WHOSE SUBJECT IS PARTLY THIS HOST. group('host') spans test.js:5957-9123 — 128 of the file's 713 ok() sites, which run 132 assertions, 30 of those sites naming an extension/{ui,offscreen}/host.js entry point in the assertion text. It installs a Chrome platform at :6608 (globalThis.chrome = { runtime: { sendMessage, onMessage, getURL } }) and asserts that THIS Host's send, onMessage, assetUrl, storage, armShortcut, transport and page really behave the way shared/host.js declares. Those are conformance claims about the extension Host, and they live inside the unit's own step because they live inside the unit's own suite file. MEASURED in #11's review, and RE-MEASURED at v0.3.1 (b9dc537, the v0.3.0 tree) because the step's count has moved twice since — every figure in this paragraph names the tree it was taken on, because the previous revision of it claimed to have been re-measured at v0.3.0 while carrying pre-v0.3.0 numbers: replacing offscreen/host.js:67 send() with a contract-satisfying non-Chrome implementation — same envelope, same undefined return, same swallowed delivery failure, delivered over a plain bus — takes step `unit` from 766 passed to 764 passed, 2 failed, both reds naming send(). A HOLE MUST IMPORT INERTLY: since v0.3.0 (#30) the group imports each hole in a try/catch, so a hole that reaches for its platform at module evaluation is a NAMED RED carrying that hole's path rather than a crash that ends the run with nothing named — and a throw anywhere else in the group reddens the assertion at its foot instead. docs/VENDORING.md carries the rule; this is the mechanism. `otherSteps` cannot carry this, because `unit` is genuinely both the unit's DSP suite and the Host's conformance suite; this key is where it is said, and tools/unit-check.mjs holds it to the code from both directions. S11 (#12) decides whether the group is split into a step of its own.

suites.why: The DSP body of evidence — WAV, the rings, the mixer, the OLA planes, cacheddeck, the scheduler — and, since S1 to S6, the scans that say the engine and the deck reach for nothing but their Host. It is the largest single suite over the unit in this repository. THE THREE READS ARE THE SEAM CHECKED FROM BOTH SIDES: it reads the extension's own ui/host.js and offscreen/host.js to assert that every duty the deck and the engine reach for is a declared one, and offscreen/host-pin.js to read the model's upstream origin out of the pin. It also walks extension/ wholesale for that last grep, host files included. WHAT A COPY ACTUALLY GETS OUT OF IT, corrected in #11's review because the first version of this sentence predicted the wrong failure: only the host-pin read can go missing. ui/host.js and offscreen/host.js are HOLES — a second product has already supplied its own files at those paths, because it cannot run at all without them — so both imports succeed and nothing here is about a file that could not be opened. What goes red instead is `hostConformance` below. None of the reads is guarded, which is still right: a read that silently skipped would report coverage it does not have. But the honest summary is that `unit` is the one step in this list a second Host cannot pass as it stands.

THE SEAM ITSELF, which is why it is the unit's and not this Host's: every file it touches is unit. It drives serialiseBackend (shared/host.js) over WorkerBackend (workers/workerbackend.js), and it reads workers/inference.worker.js AS TEXT — also unit — to check the fake port's refusal against the sentence the shipped worker really prints, and to count that the worker's `busy` guard still covers only the INFER case. So it declares no `reads`: nothing it opens is across the seam, and the completeness half in tools/unit-check.mjs is what says so rather than this sentence. IT TRAVELS, and a copy gets more out of it than out of most of this list: its last section drives the wrapper over a fake Backend that owes every duty and answers none, which is the shape a second Host's backend has on the day it is written. A product that hands the engine a backend over IPC and forgets to settle the calls in flight when dispose() kills the child process is red HERE, in the unit's own words, instead of shipping a deck that goes silent with nothing reported. Classified when #9 and #11 were integrated together; before that this list was eleven and the runner had no `seam` step.

The deck's display laws under plain node. Declared in `outside` above for the same reason it is listed here: it exercises the unit and is not part of it, and S9 (#10) left the sentence saying so pointing at this list.
The segment grid at its edges and the constants that define it. Its whole subject is shared/config.js, shared/ring.js and shared/wav.js.
QA-15 — G_PASS = min(resolved stem gains) — on the real emitter and the real mixer, engine/live.js and engine/mixer.js, no browser.

A unit file that is its own suite: `node extension/engine/pitch.js` runs the phase vocoder against itself. The file travels because it is unit; the step is here because running it is how the copy is checked.

The other half of the same file's claim, and the one that matters most to a copy: pitchbank.js is verbatim-copied into offscreen/playback-processor.js, and this suite asserts the copy still matches the source. It is a `roots` entry above for exactly that reason.
A unit file that is its own suite: chroma folding and key correlation.
A unit file that is its own suite, and chroma's only caller: the windowing, the wire payload, the reset hook.
A unit file that is its own suite: the onset envelope, the octave tie-break, beat phase.

SPEED must not move the KEY, measured through the real shifter at plus or minus 2 cents. THE TWO READS ARE THE POLICY'S OTHER END: the key-lock ruling spans the deck's ladder and the page's transport, so the suite reads the two content scripts as text to assert that no path in the extension leaves the element key-unlocked. That half of the claim is about this Host, and it does not travel.

The deck's pure state, and the largest suite the deck has. A unit file that is its own suite. Its one read of a Host file is declared TWICE, and the two answer different questions — the same shape as ui/dev/selftest.mjs being in both `outside` and `suites`. `hostReads` above asks what the UNIT FILE reaches for, and carries S10's ruling that speed.js stays behind; this `reads` asks what the SUITE opens, which is the list a copy is assembled from. #11's review found the second half missing: a consumer iterating `suites[].reads` — which is exactly what S11 (#12) is instructed to do — got six of the seven reads and would have left speed.js out of docs/VENDORING.md, so a copy would take the red the `hostReads` entry was written to explain, with nothing in the copy instructions to explain it.

runners.why: The runner. `node tools/verify.mjs --unit` builds its plan by reading the `suites` list ABOVE, out of this file, so the list IS the plan rather than a description of one — the rule tools/host.mjs and tools/fetch-model.sh already follow about the model pin. The VOID rule applies unchanged: a listed suite that exits 0 while asserting nothing is red, not green.

tools/verify.mjs imports MODEL_URL, MODEL_BYTES, MODEL_SEED_REL and modelSeed from it at module scope, so the runner does not load without it. Named here because a copy that omits it cannot run `--unit` at all — not because it is unit. Its own reach for offscreen/host-pin.js is an import rather than a text read, which is the harder kind: a copy needs this Host's pin, or its own file at that path.

otherSteps.why: node docs/snippets/selftest.js. Its subject is docs/snippets/*, the AUDIO.md reference implementations — a second, independent copy of the DSP written to be compared AGAINST the shipped code rather than to be it. Its one touch of the unit is `import { STEMS as CONFIG_STEMS } from '../../extension/shared/config.js'`, a cross-check that the document still agrees with the pin. The document does not travel.

node qa/compare.mjs smoke. Its subject is the QA testbed — the synthetic sources a separation is measured against — re-derived from WAVs on disk. It imports shared/wav.js and shared/config.js to read them, which makes the unit its tool rather than its subject.
node extension/autonav.js. autonav.js is host: a classic content script that suppresses YouTube's autoplay-next. Its suite is host-side with it.
node extension/speed.js. speed.js is host for the same reason, and its suite with it. The unit's half of the key-lock claim is `speed-pitch`, which is in the list above.

node tools/tree-check.mjs. Asks whether extension/ loads as an extension — manifest paths, one deck, no downloads permission. A question about this Host's declaration of itself, which is the one thing a second product supplies entirely.

node tools/unit-check.mjs. The gate on THIS FILE, and it cannot run in a copy: it reads the extension host's sw/service-worker.js, content.js, ui/welcome* and manifest.json by name, and none of them travels. The declaration is verified here, once, and ships verified.
node tools/name-check.mjs. Asserts the product rename finished across the tracked tree. A property of this repository's published surface.
node tools/svg-check.mjs. Asserts every tracked SVG is XML, so the mark renders through . brand/ is not unit.

node tools/model-parity.mjs. Reads the 114 MB pinned weights, which are not in git and are not copied — `heavy`, so `--quick` drops it and so does this list. Its claim about the unit (six sources in STEMS order) is real; a copy that wants it fetches the weights and runs the step by name.

node tools/backend-audio.mjs. The strongest claim about the unit anywhere in this tree — the real weights through the Host seam, six stems in STEMS order that add back up to the mix — and it is out of this list only because it is `slow` AND `heavy`: it needs a browser and the weights, and `--unit` is the plain-node plan. Run it by name after a copy, with the weights seeded.
node tools/embed-smoke.mjs. Loads the real unpacked extension into a real Chromium. There is no unpacked extension in a copy.
